global_lexicon.core_thesis: An explainable cross-plant transfer learning framework predicts transmembrane pressure in data-limited pilot-scale membrane bioreactors by leveraging LSTM models pretrained on data-rich source plants to capture shared extracellular polymeric substance patterns and adaptively recalibrating plant-specific fouling mechanisms using modest target-plant fine-tuning data.

key_terms.definition: An advanced wastewater treatment process combining biological activated sludge treatment with microfiltration or ultrafiltration membrane separation.
The pressure difference across the membrane filtration barrier, serving as the primary operational indicator of membrane fouling development under constant flux.
Biomacromolecular slime (proteins and carbohydrates) secreted by microorganisms or released by cell lysis, acting as primary foulants forming cake layers on membrane surfaces.
Carbohydrate fraction of EPS that serves as a highly conserved, transferable fouling signal across different MBR treatment plants.
Proteinaceous fraction of EPS whose fouling contribution is selectively amplified and recalibrated under iron-enriched influent conditions in the target plant.
Soluble microbial excretion and decay products that pass through microfilters or accumulate in mixed liquor, driving internal pore blocking.
Protein fraction of soluble microbial products that plays an elevated fouling role during microbial stress or shock events in industrial wastewater treatment.
A machine learning paradigm that transfers knowledge representations from data-rich source systems to improve predictive generalization in data-scarce target systems.
Adaptive recalibration of pretrained model weights using limited target-plant data (such as a 40% target fine-tuning ratio).
A recurrent neural network architecture designed to capture sequential temporal dependencies and long-term trends in dynamic membrane fouling processes.
A gradient boosted decision tree ensemble algorithm utilized as a competitive baseline and base predictive model.
A game-theoretic interpretability method that assigns each input feature an additive attribution score explaining individual and global model predictions.
A model-agnostic feature importance technique that systematically removes one input variable at a time to quantify its impact on predictive accuracy.
An unsupervised orthogonal transformation used to visualize distributional overlap, cluster boundaries, and domain shifts between source and target MBR datasets.
An in-situ chemical cleaning sequence (citric acid followed by sodium hypochlorite) used to restore membrane flux and quantify inorganic vs. organic foulant mass.

global_context_pack:
Core Thesis: An explainable cross-plant transfer learning framework predicts transmembrane pressure (TMP) in data-limited pilot-scale membrane bioreactors (MBRs) by pretraining LSTM and XGBoost models on three data-rich source plants to capture shared extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) fouling patterns and adaptively recalibrating plant-specific mechanisms with limited target-plant fine-tuning data.

Output Language: English

Glossary of Acronyms and Terms:
- MBR: Membrane Bioreactor
- TMP: Transmembrane Pressure
- EPS: Extracellular Polymeric Substances
- EPSc: Extracellular Polymeric Substance Carbohydrates / Polysaccharides
- EPSp: Extracellular Polymeric Substance Proteins
- SMP: Soluble Microbial Products
- SMPc: Soluble Microbial Product Carbohydrates
- SMPp: Soluble Microbial Product Proteins
- MLSS: Mixed Liquor Suspended Solids
- MLVSS: Mixed Liquor Volatile Suspended Solids
- HRT: Hydraulic Retention Time
- SRT: Solids Retention Time
- FLUX: Membrane Permeate Flux
- TCOD / SCOD: Total / Soluble Chemical Oxygen Demand
- LSTM: Long Short-Term Memory
- XGBoost: Extreme Gradient Boosting
- FT: Fine-Tuning
- SHAP: SHapley Additive exPlanations
- LOFO: Leave-One-Feature-Out
- PCA: Principal Component Analysis
- CIP: Clean-in-Place
- LC-OCD: Liquid Chromatography–Organic Carbon Detection
- EEM: Excitation-Emission Matrix

Document Outline & Structure:
- Abstract: Motivation of fouling prediction under data scarcity, proposed transfer learning framework, source pretraining performance, target plant fine-tuning gains, mechanistically interpretable SHAP/LOFO shifts, and industrial MBR cross-scenario validation.
- Section 1: Introduction: Operational challenges of MBR fouling, limitations of data-driven modeling in data-limited plants due to sparse EPS/SMP monitoring, promise of transfer learning, explainability requirements, and study objectives.
- Section 2: Materials and methods: Data collection across target and source pilot MBRs (2.1); physicochemical analytical assays including Lowry, Dubois, LC-OCD, and EEM (2.2); data preprocessing and feature selection (2.3); pretraining base models on source plants (2.4); baseline target model training (2.5); transfer learning fine-tuning workflows (2.6); performance evaluation metrics (2.7); and cross-scenario testing on an industrial MBR (2.8).
- Section 3: Results and discussion: Source–target feature distribution and PCA overlap analysis (3.1); construction and performance of base LSTM and XGBoost models supported by SHAP and source biomass characterization (3.2); transfer learning performance across fine-tuning ratios, model comparison, LOFO/SHAP attribution shifts, target-plant physicochemical verification of Fe-protein fouling pathways, and industrial MBR validation (3.3).
- Section 4: Implications and outlook: Practical implications for data-limited wastewater facilities, surrogate optical fouling fingerprints (UV-vis, EEM), full-scale hydrodynamics, and inorganic/organic coupling.
- Section 5: Conclusions: Summary of transferable EPS-centered fouling mechanisms, efficacy of LSTM-FT with limited calibration data, scientific interpretability of plant-adaptive feature shifts, and deployment outlook.
